title: Moving away from fossil fuels: who pays?
summary: The General Assembly debates a timeline to leave coal, oil and gas, and who should pay for it: subsidies, a loss and damage fund, climate finance, border taxes, displaced people and the duties of States.

committee.name: General Assembly: the transition away from fossil fuels and who pays (practice)
committee.conference: Practice: the transition away from fossil fuels
committee.notes: A practice draft written for class; not an adopted UN text. Positions are estimates from the linked sources.

topic.name: The transition away from fossil fuels and who pays
topic.notes: Real topic. Every country position is an estimate from the linked source, and countries without a source are left unknown.

tags.fossil_phaseout: Sets a timeline for countries to move away from coal, oil and gas
tags.subsidy_end: Ends government subsidies for fossil fuels by a fixed date
tags.loss_damage: Asks richer countries to put more money into the loss and damage fund
tags.finance_goal: Sets a much larger climate finance goal for developing countries
tags.border_tax: Encourages carbon charges on imports from countries with weaker climate rules
tags.displaced_people: Gives people displaced by climate change a legal status and safe ways to move
tags.state_duties: Backs the climate duties of States set out by the International Court of Justice

resolution.title: The transition away from fossil fuels and shared responsibility for its cost

preambular.text: Recalling the Charter of the United Nations and its purpose of achieving international cooperation in solving international problems of an economic, social or humanitarian character,

Reaffirming the Paris Agreement and its agreed goal of holding the rise in global average temperature to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels and pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees,
Recalling the finding of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change that it is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, the oceans and the land,

Recalling also General Assembly resolution 77/276 of 2023, adopted without a vote, which asked the International Court of Justice for an advisory opinion on the obligations of States in respect of climate change,
Taking note of the advisory opinion delivered by the International Court of Justice on 23 July 2025,

operative.text: Calls upon all States to publish national plans for a just and orderly transition away from fossil fuels, ending unabated coal power by 2040 and the use of oil and gas by 2050;
Decides that all States will end government subsidies for coal, oil and gas by 2030, while protecting poorer households that depend on cheap fuel;
Requests developed States to double their contributions to the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage within five years;

Urges developed States to raise climate finance for developing countries to at least 1.3 trillion United States dollars a year by 2035, well above the goal of 300 billion dollars a year agreed in 2024;
Encourages States to place a carbon charge on imports from countries with weaker climate rules, in line with trade law, so that emissions do not simply move abroad;
Requests the drafting of a framework that gives people displaced by climate change a legal status and safe ways to move, while helping them to stay in their homelands where possible;
Calls upon all States to comply with the obligations identified by the Court, including the duty to act with due diligence to prevent significant harm to the climate system;
Requests the Secretary-General to prepare a report, in consultation with Member States, on ways to help States meet those obligations.

cards.text: Calls upon all States to set national dates for leaving unabated coal power, taking account of their own circumstances and capacities;
Encourages States, on a voluntary basis, to share their plans for moving away from fossil fuels and to learn from one another;
Urges States to phase out inefficient fossil fuel subsidies over time while protecting the poorest households from higher prices;
Invites States in a position to do so to contribute voluntarily to the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage;
Decides to link a larger climate finance goal for developing countries to clear national plans for moving away from fossil fuels;
Calls upon States considering carbon charges on imports to consult developing countries first and to use part of the revenue for climate finance;
Invites States to cooperate on safe and regular ways for people displaced by climate change to move, in line with their national laws;
Requests the Secretary-General to report on how States can meet the climate obligations identified by the International Court of Justice, with support for developing countries;

events.title: Small island States appeal together
events.body: The small island developing States speak as one in the chamber and ask for a clear timeline to move away from fossil fuels.
events.teaches: Small island developing States often negotiate as a group so that their voices carry further on climate change.

events.title: A regional group compares instructions
events.body: Delegates from one regional group meet over lunch to compare their instructions and look for a shared line on the draft.
events.teaches: The five UN regional groups help their members coordinate positions before important votes.

events.title: Your capital asks for a report
events.body: Your foreign ministry wants a full report on the finance talks before you agree to anything, and drafting it takes up your morning.
events.teaches: Delegates report back to their capitals and must wait for instructions on sensitive points.

events.title: A legal expert briefs delegates
events.body: An international lawyer explains to delegates what the International Court of Justice said about the climate duties of States.
events.teaches: Advisory opinions of the International Court of Justice are not binding, but they carry great legal weight.

events.title: A side event on climate displacement
events.body: A non-governmental organisation hosts a side event where delegates talk informally about planning for people forced to move.
events.teaches: Side events let civil society inform delegates outside the formal meetings.

events.title: A co-sponsor hesitates
events.body: A co-sponsor says it may withdraw its name unless the wording on border taxes is softened, and delegates ask you to help find a compromise.
events.teaches: Co-sponsors can withdraw their support, so drafters must work to keep their coalition together.
